title: suck_pull: fetch_article drops dot-unstuffed lines without restoring original CRLF terminator
description:
suck_pull.rs fetch_article() lines 354-367: reads line with read_line, trims trailing CR/LF, un-stuffs leading dot, then appends with b'
'. This works correctly for the common case, but trims ALL trailing CR and LF characters via trim_end_matches(['', '
']), which collapses lines ending with multiple CRLFs or bare LFs. More critically, lines that originally ended with '' (i.e. body lines from a non-compliant server that sends bare LF) lose their content because trim_end_matches strips the . The correct approach is trim_end_matches(['', '
']) on the wire-protocol line (correct), but then unconditionally write CRLF back — which is what the code does. However the trimming is applied before the dot-unstuffing check, so a line like '..
' becomes '.. ' → wrong: it strips to '..', then drops first dot → '.', writes as '.
'. This is the CRLF reconstruction bug already present in a less obvious form.
